question_en: A company's effective tax rate is determined using its:
option_a: taxable income as shown on its tax ling.
option_b: income tax expense from the income statement.
option_c: taxes paid to the government during the period.
explanation_en: Effective tax rate = income tax expense / pretax income.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: A current or past loss in a tax return most likely will result in a:
option_c: neither a deferred tax asset nor a deferred tax liability.
explanation_en: A tax loss carryforward can offset future taxable income, thereby reducing taxes payable. This will be recorded as a deferred tax asset to the extent that the firm expects this to reverse in the future.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following financial ratios is least likely to be affected by classification of deferred taxes as a liability or equity?
explanation_en: The ROA will not be affected by the classification of the deferred taxes. The total assets will remain the same regardless of whether the deferred taxes are classified as a liability or equity. Return on equity and the leverage ratio (assets/equity) would both be affected.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: A firm operates in a country with a 30% enacted tax rate. The firm had pretax income of $150,000, income tax expense of $47,000, and paid $44,000 in income tax. Which of the following tax rates was most likely the highest?
explanation_en: Statutory tax rate = enacted rate of 30%. Effective tax rate = income tax expense / pretax income = $47,000 / $150,000 = 31.3%. Cash tax rate = tax paid (cash) / pretax income = $44,000 / $150,000 = 29.3%. In this case, the highest rate was the effective tax rate.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: The ratio of taxes paid to pretax income is a company's:
explanation_en: Cash tax rate = cash taxes paid / pretax income.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Gator Sarl (Gator) purchased some PP&E at the start of the period costing €21,000 with a three-year useful economic life and no residual value. Gator uses straight-line depreciation in its accounts, but the tax authorities use double declining balance. The following balances are given for carrying value and the value of the tax base over the asset's life: Year 1 Year 2 Year 3 € € € Carrying value 14,000 7,000 0 Tax base 7,000 2,333 0 Assuming a statutory tax rate of 30%, which of the following is closest to the DTL reported in Gator's balance sheet at the end of Year 2?
explanation_en: DTL = (carrying value – tax base) × statutory rate Year 2 DTL = (€7,000 – €2,333) × 0.3 = €1,400.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Harding Industrials, Inc., has a deferred tax asset of $300,000 and a deferred tax liability of $450,000 at the end of the reporting period, based on a tax rate of 20%. If the tax rate increases to 25%, what will be the most likely impact on the income statement?
explanation_en: Deferred taxes are recognized at the enacted tax rate (25%). This will give a deferred tax liability of $562,500 ($450,000 / 0.2 × 0.25) and a deferred tax asset of $375,000 ($300,000 / 0.2 × 0.25). So, the tax expense = tax payable + ΔDTL – ΔDTA, the increase in the DTL will increase the tax expense on the income statement by $112,500, and the increase in the DTA will decrease the tax expense by $75,000. Overall, the tax expense will increase, and the net income will decrease by $37,500.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is most likely to result in a deferred tax asset being created?
option_b: A decrease in the enacted tax rate.
explanation_en: Unearned revenue is usually taxable at the point of sale, even if not recognized in the income statement until a later period—resulting in higher current taxes payable, and a deferred tax asset being created. Depreciation commonly results in a deferred tax liability (e.g., when the tax return uses accelerated depreciation, while the income statement uses straight-line depreciation), although it could result in either a DTA or a DTL, depending on the method used. A decrease in the enacted tax rate will only decrease any existing deferred tax asset or liability.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en:
An analyst gathered the following information about a company:

- Pretax income = $10,000.
- Taxes payable = $2,500.
- Deferred taxes = $500.
- Tax expense = $3,000.

What is the firm's reported effective tax rate?
explanation_en: Reported effective tax rate = Income tax expense / pretax income = $3,000 / $10,000 = 30%

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: For purposes of financial analysis, an analyst should:
option_a: always consider deferred tax liabilities as a liability.
option_b: determine the treatment of deferred tax liabilities on a case-by-case basis.
option_c: always consider deferred tax liabilities as stockholder's equity.
explanation_en: For financial analysis, an analyst must decide on the appropriate treatment of deferred taxes on a case-by-case basis. These can be classified as liabilities or stockholder's equity, depending on various factors. Sometimes, deferred taxes are just ignored altogether.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is most likely to cause a difference between a firm's statutory and effective tax rates?
option_a: An increase in the deferred tax asset from the prior period, and no change in the deferred tax liability.
option_b: An increase in the actual cash paid to the tax authorities.
option_c: An increase in the tax-exempt income earned during the period.
explanation_en: An increase in the actual cash paid will change the cash tax rate, but it will not cause the statutory and effective tax rates to differ. Any changes in deferred tax assets and liabilities are because of temporary timing differences, which typically do not cause the statutory and effective tax rates to differ. Permanent differences, such as tax-exempt income, do cause these rates to differ.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements regarding deferred taxes is NOT correct?
option_a: Only those components of deferred tax liabilities that are likely to reverse should be considered a liability.
option_b: If deferred tax liabilities are not included in equity, debt-to-equity ratio will be reduced.
option_c: If deferred taxes are not expected to reverse in the future then they should be classified as equity.
explanation_en: When deferred tax liabilities are included in equity, it will reduce the debt-to-equity ratio (by increasing the denominator), in some cases considerably.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: For analytical purposes, if a deferred tax liability is expected to not be reversed, it should be treated as a(n):
explanation_en: If deferred tax liabilities are expected to never reverse, they should be treated as equity for analytical purposes.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following most accurately depicts the relationship between income tax expense and deferred taxes?
option_a: ΔDTL = tax expense – tax payable + ΔDTA.
option_b: Tax payable = tax expense + ΔDTL – ΔDTA.
option_c: ΔDTA = tax payable – tax expense – ΔDTL.
explanation_en: Tax expense = tax payable + ΔDTL – ΔDTA. Once rearranged, the correct answer is ΔDTL = tax expense – tax payable + ΔDTA.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following best describes valuation allowance? Valuation allowance is a reserve:
option_a: created when deferred tax assets are greater than deferred tax liabilities.
option_b: against deferred tax assets based on the likelihood that those assets will not be realized.
option_c: against deferred tax liabilities based on the likelihood that those liabilities will be paid.
explanation_en: Valuation allowance is a reserve against deferred tax assets based on the likelihood that those assets will not be realized. Deferred tax assets reflect the difference in tax expense and taxes payable that are expected to be recovered from future operations.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is an analyst least likely to include when analyzing trends in tax rates, given a reconciliation of statutory to effective tax rates?
option_a: Diering tax rates in dierent countries.
explanation_en: When analyzing trends in tax rates, an analyst should only include reconciliation items that are continuous in nature rather than sporadic. Tax-exempt income and differing tax rates in different countries tend to be continuous, whereas tax holiday savings tend to be sporadic.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: When analyzing a company's financial leverage, deferred tax liabilities are best classified as:
option_a: a liability or equity, depending on the company's particular situation.
option_c: neither as a liability, nor as equity.
explanation_en: The recommended analyst treatment of deferred tax liabilities is to treat them as liabilities if they are expected to reverse or as equity if they are not expected to reverse.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Last year, Schoenberg AG earned net income of €150,000, an income tax expense of €47,000, and paid tax of €51,000. What was the effective tax rate?
explanation_en: Effective tax rate = income tax expense / pretax income = €47,000 / (€150,000 + €47,000) = 23.9%. Note that you are given the net income, so add the tax expense back to find pretax income.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: While evaluating the financial statements of Omega, Inc., the analyst observes that the effective tax rate is 7% less than the statutory rate. The source of this difference is determined to be a tax holiday on a manufacturing plant located in South Africa. This item is most likely to be:
option_a: continuous in nature, so the termination date is not relevant.
option_b: sporadic in nature, and the analyst should try to identify the termination date and determine if taxes will be payable at that time.
option_c: sporadic in nature, but the effect is typically neutralized by higher home country taxes on the repatriated profits.
explanation_en: As the name suggests, a tax holiday is usually a temporary exemption from having to pay taxes in some tax jurisdiction. Because of the temporary nature, the key issue for the analyst is to determine when the holiday will terminate, and how the termination will affect taxes payable in the future.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
question_en: Under the liability method of accounting for deferred taxes, a decrease in the tax rate at the beginning of the accounting period will:
option_a: increase taxable income in the current period.
explanation_en: A decrease in the tax rate will decrease any DTAs and DTLs. This does not affect the current period's taxable income, but it decreases income tax expense in the income statement.
